Title: Victoria Nambaziira's AKU Transformation
NewsSummary: From uncertainty to expertise, Victoria credits AKU for her professional growth
NewsContent:
Victoria Nambaziira, a midwifery student at Aga Khan University's School of Nursing and Midwifery in Uganda, began her academic journey uncertain of her path. Initially planning to pursue nursing, a twist of fate led her to midwifery, a choice that would turn out to be transformative for her career.

Victoria's journey began when she hesitantly applied to AKU's midwifery programme after a colleague's encouragement. "I wanted to do nursing, but midwifery chose me," she recalls. Though initially unsure, Victoria's decision was solidified when everything seemed to fall into place.

Her academic journey wasn't without challenges. Victoria submitted the wrong transcript during the application process, but with the support of AKU's administration, she was given a second chance. "I was anxious, but the faculty and administration were incredibly supportive. They made everything easier."

Once enrolled, Victoria quickly became impressed by the accessibility and support at AKU. "The faculty were always there when you needed them. You could send an email or a message on WhatsApp, and they'd respond quickly. The resources, like the library, were fully stocked, and even if you weren't on campus, you could still get everything you needed."

Despite balancing work and studies, Victoria thrived. Working part-time at Nakasero Hospital while studying allowed her to gain hands-on experience that proved invaluable in making her a confident, capable midwife. "AKU trains you to be a professional. You learn critical thinking, clinical skills, and communication," she explains. The support from both her faculty and classmates was essential to her success.

Financial hurdles were another obstacle, but Victoria's perseverance, combined with the financial support she received through scholarships and loans, made it possible for her to continue her studies without constant worry over tuition fees.

Looking ahead, Victoria is excited about her future in maternal and neonatal health, with plans to continue helping mothers and babies. "I want to bring positive changes to the healthcare sector, particularly for children and the elderly because they are very vulnerable," she shares. "I'm also planning to pursue a master's degree in a few years."

Reflecting on her transformative time at AKU, Victoria says, "I'm a different person now. I'm more confident, knowledgeable, and ready to make a real difference in the world. Don't fear starting something new. Unless you start, you will never know."

As she prepares for convocation in February 2025, Victoria's story is a powerful reminder that with determination, support, and the right opportunities, any dream can be achieved.
